columns: reservation-date panels: month|week|bimonth, price (mean nightly $), nights (imputed booked nights), unit (city), trt (Boston=1); date-booked panels: price, nights, unit, dates (scrape period), per-city scrape-gap days, period_no, nights_diff, trt, nights_per_period; entries/exits: period, period_no, variable (city), value, trt; date_normalization: dates x city scrape-gap days
date_range: scrape periods jul_2018_aug_2018 to apr_2019_may_2019 (11 monthly scrapes, Jul 2018 - May 2019); reservation-date panels carry month 2-12 / week 8-52 without a year column (README: check-in dates Jul 2018 - Dec 2019, tax effective 1 Jan 2019); control_cities tax enactment dates 2014-2018
how_pulled: gh api repos/sideye/airbnb-occupancy-tax/contents/ (tree + metadata); then for each small file: curl -sL -o <file> https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sideye/airbnb-occupancy-tax/master/<urlencoded name>; described with python/pandas (xlsx read via zipfile sharedStrings because openpyxl is not installed); copied to the samples folder
full_dataset_size: Whole repo is ~43 MB / 30 files; everything skipped is presentation or duplicate bulk: Prelim SCM.pptx 12.1 MB, writeup.pages 9.4 MB, SCM Analysis.ipynb 1.7 MB, long_date_booked_2.numbers 0.3 MB, EDA/Validate/Extract notebooks ~0.4 MB. All data CSVs (total ~66 KB, ~1,200 rows) are already in this sample; the underlying per-listing calendar scrapes were never committed.
description: Derived panels from an economics honours thesis (2020) on Boston's 1 Jan 2019 short-term-rental occupancy tax: imputed booked nights and mean nightly price for Airbnb listings in 11 North American cities (Boston treated; Asheville, Chicago, DC, Denver, Montreal, Nashville, Quebec City, Rhode Island, SF, Twin Cities controls) at city-month, city-bimonth and city-week grain by reservation date, and city x scrape-period grain by booking date, plus listing entry/exit counts and a control-city lodging-tax rate sheet. Source is the author's own monthly calendar scrapes Jul 2018 - May 2019, cross-validated against reviews (~0.5 reviews per imputed night at the listing-month level). For ABNB an analyst would use it as an external calibration point for the reviews-based stays index (nights-per-review ratio), as a worked synthetic-control template for lodging-tax event studies, and as a small 2018-19 realised-nights/price panel for the regulatory factor database.
issues: No LICENSE file (all rights reserved by default; thesis data, cite the repo, do not redistribute). Repo dormant since 29 Apr 2020. Data are the author's own airbnb.com calendar scrapes - compute_reservations.py / compute_bookings_cutoff.py were NOT run (ToS call for a human); only the committed derived outputs were copied. Reservation-date panels lack a year column (must be inferred from README: Jul 2018 - Dec 2019 check-ins); README itself flags a TODO to reprocess all data with later cleaning rules, so the committed CSVs may predate the final filters. Small n (11 cities x 11 periods). openpyxl absent in venv, so control_cities.xlsx was inspected via raw XML only.
